A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same information-estimation and IDEAL study. Their main text, equations, figures, supplementary analyses, and methods support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: V3 reports original simulations and imaging experiments, including four application comparisons, estimator validation, and IDEAL optimization results in Figs. 3–4 and the supplement.

after.justification: V4 retains these original empirical results in Figs. 2–3 and the supplement, including reconstruction, classification, microscopy prediction, and estimator-validation outcomes.

M1.justification: The entropy-difference estimator, Gaussian and PixelCNN models, and IDEAL optimization procedure are retained. V4 clarifies the distinction between the Gaussian optimization objective and PixelCNN validation; both were already documented in v3's Methods.

E1.justification: Coverage remains Gehler-Shi photography, synthetic black holes, CIFAR10 lensless reconstruction and classification, BSCCM microscopy, MNIST validation, and synthetic Gaussian/1D scenarios. Dataset license disclosures and relocation of the two-point example introduce no new coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same CFA designs, telescope configurations, lens/microlens/diffuser encoders, illumination patterns, and estimator comparisons. Newly cited mutual-information estimators are discussed but are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Application-specific splits, patch sizes, noise conditions, metrics, optimization settings, and testing procedures are retained. V4's explicit separation of training and held-out samples clarifies the existing protocol; the additional resource information does not establish changed experimental settings.

E4.justification: Patch-size, sample-size, photon-count, non-Gaussian-data, encoder-uncertainty, and task-specific classification analyses are retained. The consistency subsection loses its heading but keeps its analysis and figure. V3's two-point example and Fig. 2 move to v4's S1.2 and Fig. S3.

E5.justification: Bootstrap confidence intervals, repeated-fit practices, and replicate counts remain unchanged, including 20 CFA replicates, four lensless PixelCNN fits, and 15 microscopy train-test splits. No new uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: V4 newly reports numerical computational costs in S6, including approximately 3 hours and 1 GB for IDEAL training and approximately 10 seconds per black-hole reconstruction on CPU. The matched information, reconstruction-quality, and classification figures retain their results and trends.

T1.justification: The formal models, entropy derivations, two-point analysis, and estimation-theory inequalities are retained. The clearer main-text equality I(O;Y) = I(X;Y) for deterministic encoding was already established in v3's S1.1. Equation renumbering and splitting the cross-entropy display add no theory.

C1.justification: Both versions claim measurement-and-noise-based information estimation without ground truth, validation across four imaging applications, and information-maximizing design through IDEAL. The rewritten abstract, introduction, and discussion preserve these contributions and their scope.

C2.justification: V4 explicitly states that high information content still requires suitable decoding algorithms and expands future directions involving transformers and scaling-based entropy extrapolation. Existing task-specific and calibration limitations remain, while the explicit call to validate computational advantages more broadly is removed.

D1.justification: S6 adds hardware, memory, runtime, and dataset license information for retained experiments. It removes the generic PixelCNN 20×20 training-patch statement while retaining application-specific sizes. Core implementation details, hyperparameters, and code access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V4 adds references and discussion concerning contemporary high-dimensional mutual-information estimation, autoregressive scaling, and DenseNet. This expands supporting context while retaining the original positioning relative to information theory, estimation theory, compressed sensing, and end-to-end imaging design.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, estimator explanation, model discussion, and concluding discussion receive substantial rewriting. Numbered main sections replace the Results hierarchy, the two-point example moves into the supplement, and Methods becomes the numbered S6 section with detailed subsections.

P2.justification: A new typographic format substantially resizes and reflows figures and captions throughout the paper. The application figure and caption now share a page, supplementary figures are consolidated, and the two-point figure moves to the supplement. Metric headings are refined while plotted results remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V4 clarifies held-out estimation and Gaussian-objective/PixelCNN validation, adds useful resource and licensing details, and explicitly distinguishes information capture from decoding. These modestly improve interpretability and reproducibility. The scientific validation remains unchanged, while smaller figures and removal of the call for broader efficiency validation temper the gains.
